## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A single-fascicle prose treatise by [陳那菩薩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B3%E9%82%A3%E8%8F%A9%E8%96%A9) **Dignāga** (c. 480–540), translated by [義淨](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%BE%A9%E6%B7%A8) **Yìjìng** in the early-eighth-century Táng. Preserved in the *Taishō* at T31n1622. One of the principal short Yogācāra-Madhyamaka treatises in the Chinese canon, demonstrating that all conventional designations (*prajñapti*) are constructed by *adopting* (*upādāya* = *qǔyīn* 取因) certain factors as their causal basis — neither identical with nor different from those factors.

**Abstract**

The *Qǔyīn jiǎshè lùn* is the canonical Indian Yogācāra-school formulation of *upādāya-prajñapti* doctrine: the three-fold analysis of how all conventionally-designated objects (chariot, person, time-span) reduce to constructed designations on causal bases that are neither identical with nor different from the constructed object. The doctrine is doctrinally adjacent to Madhyamaka (the *Mūla-madhyamaka-kārikā* 24's treatment of conventional truth) but is presented within the Yogācāra apparatus of *vijñapti-mātra*.

The treatise was translated by [義淨](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%BE%A9%E6%B7%A8) in his productive Chángān decades (700–711) alongside the related Dignāga short works [KR6n0119](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0119) *Zhǎngzhōng lùn*, [KR6n0121](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0121) *Guān zǒngxiàng lùn sòng*, and the Dharmapāla commentary [KR6n0113](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0113) *Guān suǒyuán lùn shì*. Together these constitute Yìjìng's principal contribution to the Chinese transmission of the Dignāga corpus, complementing the earlier work of [真諦](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%9C%9F%E8%AB%A6) and the parallel work of [玄奘](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%84%E5%A5%98).
